# Kiln

> Compile-time CRUD generation for Kotlin Multiplatform SQLite via KSP.
> Annotate a data class, rebuild, get a full type-safe repository.
> No SQL to write, no cursor mapping, no versioned migration files.

Docs: https://sufarook.github.io/Kiln/
Source: https://github.com/sufarook/Kiln
Version: 1.0.0-alpha08

## Setup (one line)

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.sufarook.kiln") version "1.0.0-alpha08"
}
```

The plugin applies KSP, wires the processor, and adds annotations + runtime
dependencies automatically.

## Annotations

### @DbEntity(tableName: String = "")
Marks a data class as a database table. Must be a data class with a primary
constructor. All constructor properties become columns unless annotated @Ignore.

### @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate: Boolean = false)
Designates a primary-key column. autoGenerate requires Long or Int type and
the property must default to 0. Two or more @PrimaryKey properties form a
composite primary key (autoGenerate not allowed on composites).

### @Column(name: String = "", unique: Boolean = false, index: Boolean = false, migrateFrom: String = "")
Overrides column name, adds constraints, or hints migration.
- name: SQL column name (default: property name)
- unique: UNIQUE constraint
- index: CREATE INDEX on this column
- migrateFrom: old column name for data-preserving rename

### @Ignore
Excludes a property from the schema. The property MUST have a Kotlin default
value. Not stored, not read from cursor.

### @Relation(cascade: Boolean = false)
Marks a foreign-key property. Generates findBy<Parent>, observeBy<Parent>,
deleteBy<Parent> on the child repository. Parent name is inferred by stripping
trailing "Id" from property name (projectId -> Project). cascade is
documentation only — no runtime FK enforcement.

## Generated Repository Methods

For each @DbEntity class, Kiln generates <Entity>Repository(driver: KilnDriver):

### Schema
- createTable() — CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + auto-migration
- KilnSchema.createAll(driver) — creates all tables in the module

### CRUD
- suspend insert(entity: T) — does NOT return generated id
- suspend insertAll(entities: List<T>) — batch insert in single transaction
- suspend update(entity: T) — updates by primary key
- suspend delete(id: ID) — deletes by primary key

### Queries
- suspend findById(id: ID): T? — null if not found
- suspend findAll(): List<T> — all rows (no guaranteed order)
- suspend findWhere(orderBy, limit, offset) { predicate }: List<T>
- suspend count(): Long
- suspend count { predicate }: Long
- suspend deleteWhere { predicate }: Int — returns deleted count

### Reactive (Flow)
- fun observeAll(): Flow<List<T>> — re-emits on every write
- fun observeWhere(orderBy, limit, offset) { predicate }: Flow<List<T>>

### @Relation Helpers (per FK property)
- suspend findBy<Parent>(parentId): List<T>
- fun observeBy<Parent>(parentId): Flow<List<T>>
- suspend deleteBy<Parent>(parentId)

### Ordering and Pagination
findWhere and observeWhere accept these optional parameters:
- orderBy: List<OrderSpec> — use Column.asc() or Column.desc()
- limit: Long = 0 — max rows (0 = no limit)
- offset: Long = 0 — rows to skip

```kotlin
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.asc
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.desc

repo.findWhere(
    orderBy = listOf(ProductColumns.price.desc()),
    limit = 20, offset = 40
) { ProductColumns.isActive eq true }
```

## DSL Operators

Used inside findWhere, observeWhere, deleteWhere, count lambdas.
All values are bound as ? parameters (SQL injection impossible).

| Operator         | SQL                    | Import needed |
|------------------|------------------------|---------------|
| col eq value     | col = ?                | eq            |
| col neq value    | col != ?               | neq           |
| col lt value     | col < ?                | lt            |
| col lte value    | col <= ?               | lte           |
| col gt value     | col > ?                | gt            |
| col gte value    | col >= ?               | gte           |
| col.between(a,b) | col BETWEEN ? AND ?    | between       |
| col inList list  | col IN (?,?...)        | inList        |
| col notInList l  | col NOT IN (?,?...)    | notInList     |
| col.isNull()     | col IS NULL            | (none)        |
| col.isNotNull()  | col IS NOT NULL        | (none)        |
| col like pat     | col LIKE ?             | like          |
| col notLike pat  | col NOT LIKE ?         | notLike       |
| pred1 and pred2  | (p1) AND (p2)          | (none)*       |
| pred1 or pred2   | (p1) OR (p2)           | (none)*       |
| not(pred)        | NOT (pred)             | not           |

*IMPORTANT: `and` and `or` are MEMBER FUNCTIONS on Predicate, not top-level
imports. They work as infix calls without import. Only `not` needs an import.

Import pattern:
```kotlin
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.eq
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.like
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.not  // only `not` needs import
// `and` / `or` are members — do NOT import them
```

## Supported Types

| Kotlin type                      | SQLite type |
|----------------------------------|-------------|
| String                           | TEXT        |
| Int, Long, Short                 | INTEGER     |
| Double, Float                    | REAL        |
| Boolean                          | INTEGER     |
| ByteArray                        | BLOB        |
| kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate       | TEXT        |
| kotlinx.datetime.LocalDateTime   | TEXT        |
| kotlinx.datetime.Instant         | TEXT        |
| Any enum class                   | TEXT        |
| Any of the above as nullable (?) | same + NULL |

## Transactions

```kotlin
import io.github.sufarook.kiln.runtime.withTransaction

driver.withTransaction {
    repo1.insert(entity1)
    repo2.update(entity2)
}
```

- Atomic commit/rollback
- Reactive flows get ONE emission after commit (not per operation)
- Blocks nest (inner joins outer; only outermost commits)
- Pass Dispatchers.IO for I/O-heavy transactions

## Auto-migration

Migration is VERSION-LESS. No migration files, no version numbers.
createTable() calls SchemaMigrator.sync() which diffs PRAGMA table_info
against the entity definition.

| Change          | Path   | What happens                              |
|-----------------|--------|-------------------------------------------|
| Add column      | Fast   | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT ...    |
| Rename column   | Slow   | Table recreated; use @Column(migrateFrom) |
| Remove column   | Slow   | Table recreated without the column        |
| Type change     | Slow   | Table recreated with CAST                 |
| No change       | No-op  | Only a PRAGMA read                        |

IMPORTANT: New non-nullable columns MUST have a Kotlin default value.
Without migrateFrom, a rename looks like drop + add (data lost).
Table renames are NOT supported (no migrateFrom on @DbEntity).

## Raw SQL Escape Hatch

For aggregates, JOINs, GROUP BY — use the driver directly:

```kotlin
val total = driver.executeQuery(
    null,
    "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM payments WHERE status = ?",
    mapper = { cursor -> cursor.next(); cursor.getDouble(0) ?: 0.0 },
    parameters = 1
) { bindString(0, "COMPLETED") }
```

WARNING: Raw writes (driver.execute) do NOT trigger KilnListener.
Call driver.notifyListeners("table_name") after raw writes if you
need reactive flows to re-emit.

## Driver Factories

| Platform | Factory                    | Usage                        |
|----------|----------------------------|------------------------------|
| Android  | AndroidDatabaseDriverFactory | .create(context, "app.db")  |
| iOS      | IosDatabaseDriverFactory    | .create("app.db")           |
| JVM      | JvmDatabaseDriverFactory    | .create("app.db")           |
| Tests    | JvmDatabaseDriverFactory    | .createInMemory()           |

## Critical Invariants

1. Kiln emits NO FOREIGN KEY constraints. @Relation generates helper methods
   only. SQLite has no idea the tables relate. Referential integrity is your
   responsibility.

2. createTable() order does not matter — no FK dependencies between tables.

3. KilnSchema.createAll(driver) covers every @DbEntity in a module.
   Prefer it over per-repository createTable() calls.

4. All repositories sharing the same KilnDriver share the same KilnListener.
   Use ONE driver instance. Separate drivers = broken reactive observation.

5. createTable() MUST be called outside any transaction — it throws
   IllegalStateException if called inside one.

6. insert() does not return the generated id. Query by a unique field
   after insert if you need the id.

7. Empty list to inList/notInList throws IllegalArgumentException.
   Guard with if (list.isNotEmpty()).
